name: Refugee/Asylum Status

requirements.blocker_text: The UAE is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol and has no formal domestic asylum system or refugee-status determination framework. The UAE does not use the term 'refugee' in its immigration framework and does not grant Convention rights. Some UNHCR-registered individuals are hosted informally, and humanitarian residency is granted case-by-case at the government's discretion, but there is no route to apply for asylum in the UAE.

sources.title: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security — general immigration framework (absence of any refugee/asylum provisions confirmed by omission across all ICP policy pages)

notes: SAME STRUCTURAL PATTERN as sg_asylum, the only other 'no formal system' case in this dataset — modeled using status: closed with superseded_by explicitly null, representing 'this genuinely does not exist' rather than 'this existed and stopped.' The UAE DOES host some UNHCR-registered individuals informally and grants humanitarian residency case-by-case at government discretion — a slightly more accommodating informal posture than Singapore's, where no such informal mechanism was confirmed during research — but neither country has anything resembling a formal, rights-based asylum system, and neither should be modeled as having one.
